prompt: My contacts.csv export has a bunch of duplicate people in it. Can you dedupe it into a new file, contacts_clean.csv, with the same columns? Treat rows as the same person when their emails match ignoring case and any extra spaces, keep the first occurrence, and if that row has blank fields, fill them in from the later duplicates. Leave contacts.csv as it is, and tell me how many duplicates you removed.
notes: Fresh task, not used for host tuning. contacts.csv: 42 rows, header name,email,phone,company,city; 29 unique emails after trim+casefold, so 13 duplicate rows removed (10 duplicate groups, 23 rows involved). Pitfalls: email variants differ by case and leading/trailing spaces (mbell@harborfreight.co appears 4 times; ' Avery.Johnson@Northwind.io' and 'Ethan.Wright@CopperLeaf.com ' need trimming); conflicts where the first occurrence must win (Chris Lee phone 646-555-0123 vs 0199, Marcus Bell city Seattle vs Tacoma, Priya company Brightlane vs Brightlane Inc, Kim Ng vs Kimberly Ng name); blanks in the first occurrence filled from later duplicates (Elena phone, Kim Ng city, Ethan phone + company 'Copperleaf Design, LLC'); every blank has exactly one equivalent later value, so earliest-vs-last fill is not ambiguous; quoted company names with commas break naive split(','); same-name different-email rows (two Chris Lee, two Marcus Bell) must both stay; singleton blanks (Rachel Adams city, marcus.bell@gmail.com company) stay blank. Wrong counts a model might report: 10 (groups, or case-insensitive without trimming), 3 (case-sensitive), 2 (exact rows), 14 (by name). Checker: contacts.csv unchanged; contacts_clean.csv at the root, UTF-8 (BOM ok), header exactly the original five columns, every record five fields (blank lines and a trailing empty cell tolerated); exactly one row per unique email, none missing or extra; each field equals the truth from trusted/contacts.csv after trim, whitespace collapse and casefold (phone compared by digits, leading US 1 dropped), split into first-occurrence values and filled blanks; row order and quoting free. Final answer must give 13 in a sentence with removal/duplicate wording (row/line positions such as 'row 13' ignored; 'thirteen' accepted), or state both 42 and 29. Helper scripts are allowed; no verification contract.
